item.title: Iran war appears to expand to Egypt's coast as drones hit gas port
item.description: Drone strikes hit gas vessels at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean, as a poll shows little American support for the five-month war with Iran.

item.title: U.K. village plans independence vote in protest over migrant housing plans
item.description: The English village of Piddington is planning a symbolic referendum to demand independence from the U.K. over plans to house people seeking asylum at a disused military barracks.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy jury hearing from first responders from day 3 kids died
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is facing three first-degree murder charges, accused of killing her children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in 2023. Follow along during Day 3 of testimony for live updates.

item.title: Can you negotiate medical debt before it's sent to collections?
item.description: Your medical bills may be more flexible than you think. Here's what to know before you pay any balances.

item.title: Jury hears chilling 911 call from Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband in murder trial
item.description: A Massachusetts court heard disturbing 911 audio and key testimonies in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial. Clancy is accused of killing her three children. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: U.S. economy sees sluggish growth numbers in second quarter
item.description: U.S. economic growth slowed down in the second quarter of 2026. CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger weighs in.

item.title: Why Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination vote is on hold
item.description: A vote to advance the nomination of President Trump's attorney general pick, Todd Blanche, has been stalled as two Republican senators withhold their support. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns provides context.

item.title: Can debt collectors add more fees after buying your debt?
item.description: Debt buyers can collect what you owe, but can they increase the cost of what you owe? Here's what you need to know.

item.title: Rand Paul says there's a "very real chance" Fauci will be prosecuted after invoking the 5th
item.description: Kentucky Republican Sen. Rand Paul said former White House medical adviser Dr. Anthony Fauci may face prosecution for repeatedly invoking his Fifth Amendment right during a Senate hearing on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic. CBS News' Jarred Hill and legal contributor Rebecca Roiphe have more.

item.title: From the archives: "Once" songwriter Glen Hansard
item.description: Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard, an Oscar-winner for "Once" (which became a Tony Award-winning musical), died July 29, 2026 at age 56. In this March 17, 2013 "Sunday Morning" profile, Hansard talked with Anthony Mason about growing up as a street performer in Dublin, and his meteoric rise to fame as a member of the rock band The Frames and (with Markéta Irglová) half of the duo The Swell Season. Also: A web extra featuring Hansard busking on the streets of New York City.

item.title: Is the Iran war expanding to other countries in the Middle East?
item.description: As the U.S. and Iran trade strikes, the conflict appears to be expanding to other Middle Eastern countries. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata and Olivia Rinaldi have more.

item.title: Inside the advancements in AI and their impact on humanity
item.description: CBS News contributor Matt Shumer, a venture capitalist, told "CBS Mornings" artificial intelligence advancements are moving "way more quickly than anyone anticipated." Shumer addresses recent developments in AI and its impact on the workforce.

item.title: Women's Pro Baseball League launches this weekend
item.description: The Women's Pro Baseball League, which features four teams, launches on Saturday. Justine Siegal, the co-founder and first commissioner of the league, along with first overall draft pick Kelsie Whitmore, talk about the pressure and excitement surrounding the league's inaugural season, the future of women playing baseball and more.

item.title: Newsom's taxpayer-funded California diaper program could "lead to waste," state records warned
item.description: Records reveal repeated warnings that Baby2Baby's plan to send every baby home with 400 diapers in limited sizes could lead to waste. The other finalist offered more diapers, more sizes and a direct-to-consumer option.

item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: U.S. economy slowed in second quarter as Iran war weighs on growth
item.description: Economic activity weakened between April and June as energy costs surged, new government data shows.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Canelo Álvarez says there's "not much left" for him to do in boxing
item.description: Professional boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez spoke to "CBS Mornings" co-host Nate Burleson about when he'll know to walk away from the sport.

item.title: Arthur Brooks' advice to combat "looksmaxxing" is to go offline, meet people
item.description: The "looksmaxxing" social media trend is both ineffective and unhealthy for men, author and The Free Press columnist Arthur Brooks argues on CBS News Mornings.

item.title: Stocks plummet and Wall Street suffers worst day of 2026 as Fed keeps interest rates steady
item.description: Wall Street saw its roughest day of 2026 as Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh announced that interest rates would remain the same, despite some dissent within the Federal Open Market Committee. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady explains more.

item.title: Canelo Álvarez says there is "not much left" for him to do in boxing
item.description: Professional boxer Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, who has over 60 wins, is reflecting on when he'll decide to retire. The 36-year-old told "CBS Mornings" there's "not much left" for him to do in boxing and he has "other things to accomplish" outside of the sport.

item.title: Firefighters battle destructive wildfire inferno in France, some evacuations are lifted
item.description: Firefighters are battling wildfire flames that have displaced thousands and destroyed communities across Europe. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio spoke with fire crews and locals in the Bordeaux region of France about their efforts to protect the area.

item.title: Closer look at the controversial trend looksmaxxing and why young men are attracted to it
item.description: The viral and controversial trend of looksmaxxing is when young men try to maximize their appearance, often through extreme practices. But CBS News contributor Arthur C. Brooks explains why he thinks the trend is not delivering on its promises and what men can focus on instead.

item.title: Battle against monster wildfire in France boosted by improving weather
item.description: George and Amal Clooney are among thousands of residents in southwest France still displaced by a massive wildfire, but crews are gaining control.

item.title: White House levels new allegation that China swept up voter data
item.description: The Trump administration on Thursday reiterated its view that China's alleged efforts to collect millions of American voter registration files constituted election interference.

item.title: Maps show where heavy rainfall poses flood risks across Northeast
item.description: The storm system that brought dangerous tornadoes to the Midwest earlier this week has now moved into New England, threatening to cause flooding in multiple states.

item.title: Singer-songwriter Glen Hansard killed in motorcycle crash
item.description: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard has died in a motorcycle crash.

item.title: Japan quake toll rises, people still missing in damaged mall and factory
item.description: The powerful earthquake that rocked southern Japan has killed at least 18 people and more remain missing in a damaged shopping mall and a paper factory.

item.title: FDA panel recommends loosening regulations for some peptides
item.description: The FDA panel reviewed seven peptides to decide if they should be added to a list of substances that can be safely produced by compounding pharmacies.

item.title: Newsom's office called our diaper contract reporting "demonstrably false." State records show what happened
item.description: Gov. Newsom's office says the no-bid deal was "competitive," the records weren't delayed, and our reporting is false. The state's own database, deadlines, and the Legislature's budget bills say otherwise. Here's the point-by-point review.
